text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA

- A majority stake in Romanian cement maker Romcim will be sold in August to one of five bidders, including Spain's Valenciena Cementos, France's Lafarge SA, British RMC Group and Germany's Heidelberger Zement, the newspaper says.
ADEVARUL

- The National Privatisation Agency drafted a bill saying former owners of banks, factories, hotels, hospitals, mines, whose properties were confiscated by the Communist regime would get compensation in the form of shares.
- The Labour, Health and Education Ministries will get more funds after the budget revision now being considered. Other ministries will have their allocations cut.
- After rainfalls at the weekend, the wheat crop still to be harvested wil he halved, the newspaper says.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Wage indexation will be around 15-20 percent for the second half of 1997, according to negotiations with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the newspaper says.
- Romania will need more money from international lenders to cover its social security needs. the newspaper quotes Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara as saying.
- Private bank Banca Internationala a Religiilor to increase its capital to 80 billion lei from 43.8 billion lei previously.

- Romania's flag carrier Tarom will be able to purchase two new Boeing aircraft in the year 2000 as part of plans to renew its fleet. The airline has a deal with Boeing to purchase eight planes over the next few years.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Railway passenger and freight fares rose by 15 percent and 6.7 percent, starting August 4.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romania needs reforms in the financial services sector, especially in banking and insurance, Karen Fogg, head of the European Union's mission in Romania, is quoted as saying.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The government has allocated nine billion lei worth of food and clothing for thousands of Romanian families affected by floods in the past two weeks.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Employees at the rolling stock manufacturer Astra Vagoane SA stopped work briefly to protest against the SNCFR railway authority's failure to pay 118 billion lei in debts.
- Romania's exiled King Mihai has started a one-month private holiday in Romania on Monday and will tour the country's western and northern regions.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The southern counties of Prahova and Dimbovita were badly affected by rainfall in the past two days with more than 2,400 houses destroyed by landslides or high water.
- Dozens of people in the northern region of Maramures and the central city of Brasov were taken to hospital with mushroom poisoning. More than half of them were children.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
